payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-22
payload.summary:
**Agents are swallowing the stack**; **Google's Gemini play is shifting from model to harness**, with Logan Kilpatrick describing an "Antigravity" layer meant to power coding, search, and consumer agents alike; builders across X keep circling the same pressure point: context beats prompts, routing beats monoliths, and headless software may become the real enterprise battleground.

**The builder feed had bite today**; **Vercel and Cursor people obsessed over craft and performance**, OpenAI folks asked where Codex still feels rough, and several investors and operators zeroed in on the strange new economics of token plans, personal context, and agents that may soon touch more data in a query than a human does in a month.

**今天最硬的线索还是 agent 在吞整条工具链**；**Logan Kilpatrick 说得很直白，Google 不只想卖模型，还想把 agent 的那层“harness”铺进编码、搜索和 Gemini 产品里**；X 上一圈人也在往同一个点上收：上下文比提示词更要命，路由层开始冒头，软件一旦变成“给 agent 用”，企业侧的玩法就要重写。

**这波动态也不只是空喊概念**；**Vercel、Cursor 这帮人盯的是手感、性能、完成度**，OpenAI 在追问 Codex 哪儿还不顺手；另一边，投资人和产品人已经在聊更现实的事：token 到底该怎么花，个人上下文值不值钱，agent 一次任务可能会翻的数据，真能比人一个月摸过的还多。

sections.headline: **Google** says the harness now matters as much as the model; **Google** 把重心从模型推到 agent harness
sections.body:
In this **Training Data** episode, **Logan Kilpatrick** lays out how **Google** is moving past the old "model as the through line" story. His argument is that **Gemini** was step one; now the real unifier is the agent harness behind **Antigravity**, which stretches across an IDE, web experience, CLI, SDK, **AI Studio**, Search, and the **Gemini** app. The framing is blunt: coding turned out to be a strong general-purpose harness, not just a coding feature.

He also draws a line between near-term product caution and long-term ambition. **Google** is still in "crawl" mode for most products, with the **Gemini** app closer to "walk," because mainstream users still want to stay in the driver's seat. On business tradeoffs, Kilpatrick pushes a clear view: success is about outcomes, not maximizing eyeballs. If agents do more on a user's behalf, **Google** would rather that increase total value than keep people parked in interfaces.

这期 **Training Data** 里，**Logan Kilpatrick** 把 **Google** 的路数说得挺明白：以前大家讲的是“模型是主线”，现在主线开始变成 agent 的 harness。按他的说法，**Gemini** 只是第一层，下一层是 **Antigravity** 这套底盘，往外接 IDE、网页端、CLI、SDK，再一路接进 **AI Studio**、Search 和 **Gemini** app。重点不在“会写代码”本身，而在编码这件事意外长成了一种通用 agent 框架。

他对产品节奏也没打鸡血。大部分 **Google** 产品还在“crawl”阶段，真正接近“walk”的更像 **Gemini** app，因为普通用户暂时还不想把方向盘彻底交出去。至于业务上的自我蚕食，他的说法很直接：别盯着停留时长，先看结果。要是 agent 真能把事办掉，那就让它办，不用非把人困在界面里。

sections.headline: HTML becomes the substrate for agentic video; **HTML** 被拉进 agent 视频制作底层
sections.body:
Why HTML turned out to be the foundation for agentic video making from @liu8in:

“We’ve been trying to build a video agent. However, we learned the hard way that agents have no visual intelligence.

So that’s when we turned to code. HTML is the LLM’s native language. LLMs can express not only information, but also visual aesthetics through HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Footage, images, assets, SVGs can all sit on top of HTML.”

📌 As an example, see how you can make a product video from any website URL here: https://t.co/Q2p8XzCfc6

@liu8in 解释了为什么 **HTML** 最后成了 agent 视频制作的底层：

“我们一直想做一个视频 agent。但后来硬碰硬地发现，agent 根本没有视觉智能。

所以我们转去写代码。**HTML** 是 LLM 的母语。LLM 不只会用 **HTML**、**CSS** 和 **JavaScript** 表达信息，也能借它们表达视觉审美。

素材、图片、资源、SVG，都可以叠在 **HTML** 上面。”

📌 这里有个例子，演示怎么从任意网站 URL 做出产品视频：https://t.co/Q2p8XzCfc6

sections.headline: **Sakana's Fugu** pushes model routing into one API; **Sakana Fugu** 想把多模型调度塞进单一接口
sections.body:
Another new idea to push the state of AI architectures forward. Sakana released a model that effectively uses a mixture of models to get work done. You get a single API but then the work gets farmed out the model that best performs the task. 

“Fugu manages model selection, delegation, verification, and synthesis automatically. It solves tasks directly when that is enough, or coordinates a team of expert models when a problem calls for more. The complexity of a multi-agent system never reaches your code.”

This is generally how applied AI products are building their agent harnesses at this point, but the idea of making this an LLM that any developer can interact with is also a great idea. As we get more innovation with both frontier closed and OSS models, there’s going to be a ton of value produced for the layer that can route the best.

又来了个把 AI 架构往前推一步的新点子。**Sakana** 发了一个模型，本质上是靠多模型协作来把活干完。你面对的是一个 API，但具体任务会被分发给最适合它的模型。

“**Fugu** 会自动处理模型选择、委派、验证和综合。任务简单时它自己做；问题更复杂时，它会拉起一组专家模型协作。多 agent 系统的复杂度不会直接砸到你的代码上。”

现在很多应用型 AI 产品做 agent harness，本来就差不多是这个思路；但把这层做成任何开发者都能直接交互的 LLM，本身也是个很好的方向。等前沿闭源模型和开源模型继续往外冒，最能把路由做好的那一层，会吃到不少价值。

sections.headline: Headless agents may become the biggest enterprise users; 无头 agent 可能很快成为企业软件的头号用户
sections.body:
Agents will use software 100X more than people. 

When that happens, theres a huge need for guardrails on what the agents are doing so they don’t leak data or change the wrong information, authoritative sources of truth for them to work with, logging and auditing of what they’re doing, the ability to collaborate with people through these systems, and more.

A simple query on any given agentic task could pull in more data than a user touches in a month. As a result, there are lots of categories of software that when it goes headless that the usage and value go up substantially. Agents will end up using our CRM data, documents and corporate knowledge, analytics data, and other information far more than people ever did.

The platforms that can move toward the model of powering these headless interactions, and have a business model and technology strategy to support this, will be in the best position in the future.

agent 用软件的频率会比人高出 100 倍。

真到了那一步，就会特别需要护栏：得防它们泄露数据、改错信息；得给它们权威真源；得有日志和审计；还得让它们能通过这些系统和人协作，等等。

一个看起来很简单的 agent 任务查询，拉进来的数据量，可能就比一个用户一个月摸过的还多。结果就是，很多软件类别一旦变成无头调用，使用量和价值都会明显往上走。agent 最后会比人更频繁地去用我们的 CRM 数据、文档、企业知识、分析数据，以及其他各种信息。

谁能把这种无头交互跑起来，同时业务模式和技术策略也跟得上，谁以后的位置就会更好。

sections.headline: Longer context beats slop-prone short prompts; 输入太短，AI slop 基本躲不过
sections.body:
A good rule of thumb for preventing AI slop (in writing, design, etc):

Is your input (the context) longer than the output? 

I've found that for the AI to produce quality results, my input is often 3-5 times the length of the output.

If your input is much shorter than the output, it's almost certainly going to produce slop

防止 AI slop（不管是写作还是设计）有个挺好用的经验法则：

你的输入（也就是上下文）是不是比输出更长？

我发现，要让 AI 产出像样的结果，我的输入通常得是输出长度的 3 到 5 倍。

如果你的输入远短于输出，那基本八九不离十会产出 slop。
